root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `pj_projection_specific_setup_geos()` can fall through to `if (P->phi0 != 0.0)`, the already-computed `Q->h` must be positive. When `Q->h <= 0.`, the destructor path at line 200 must not continue into later reads from `P`.
root_cause_criterion.description: The malformed `h\xff\xff` token makes `Q->h` default to 0.0 on the crashing path. The vulnerable build still reaches the `P->phi0` read with that unmet guard, while the fixed original returns during cleanup and the `h_eq_1_boundary` perturbation supplies the genuine witness where the fixed build reaches the same sink site with `Q->h = 1`.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The fixed original case is guarded because it still computes `Q->h = 0` but returns from the cleanup path before `phi0_read_sink`; the closest source-grounded perturbation `h_eq_1_boundary` executes the protected event with `Q->h = 1` and verifies the positive-height witness.

nodes.state: Inside the `Q->h <= 0.` branch, `pj_default_destructor(P, PJD_ERR_H_LESS_THAN_ZERO)` frees the live `PJ` object while the local variable `P` still names that allocation.
The immediate fallthrough after the destructor reaches `if (P->phi0 != 0.0)` while `P` still equals the just-freed `PJ`, so the branch condition performs the ASan-reported heap-use-after-free read.

edges.relation: The same `Q->h` value observed at the height guard is carried into the error-cleanup branch. When that value is non-positive, execution enters the destructor call instead of taking the only safe path to later `P` field reads.
The exact `P` pointer passed into `pj_default_destructor` at line 200 is still the pointer whose `phi0` field is read at line 202, so the sink executes after the free on the same `PJ` allocation.
